body:
kevin: Heads up — us-west GPU pools are hitting sustained saturation after the marketing batch embed job started. gpu_util=98%, queue_len≈720, p99gen=2.1s, spillover_ratio=0.62. We’re seeing a lot of tenant-tiered requests queued which is blowing past the admission window.

sylvie: ack. any single tenant causing this or many small ones? :eyes:

kevin: it’s a mix — big batch from customer-A and a surge of free-tier embedding churn from anonymizer jobs. traffic pattern: long-seq embeddings + frequent short chat requests.

raj: can we throttle the free tier at the ingress and prefer cross-region spillover to eu-west instead of local queueing? cost tradeoff is network egress vs GPU queue time.

maria: +1 to ingress throttling. also propose model fallback for large embeddings: route to quantized-embedding-2 (smaller model) for non-SLA customers. saves ~3x tokens/GPU cycles.

kevin: quick proposal I sketched:
```yaml
admission_control:
  global_gpu_headroom_pct: 8
  per_tenant_token_rate_limit:
    free: 40rps
    standard: 200rps
    pro: 1000rps
  spillover_policy:
    prefer_regions: [eu-west-1, ap-south-1]
    max_cross_region_ratio: 0.4
fallbacks:
  embeddings:
    - match: {tier: free}
      model: quantized-embedding-2
      allowed: true
  generate:
    - match: {latency_tier: best_effort}
      model: llama2-7b-quant
      allowed: true
```

raj: that looks sane. two notes: 1) we need to keep per-tenant fairness — add a sliding window so a single customer-A batch doesn’t exhaust free burst tokens; 2) make cross-region preference metric-aware (latency SLA + egress cost).

maria: add a short-circuit for cached prefixes: if kv_cache hit rate > 20% serve from cache even if queue > threshold. reduces cost.

ops-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-3078 — us-west GPU saturation. Linked runbook: /runbooks/egress-spillover.

kevin: action items:
- raj: update ingress admission controller to enforce per_tenant sliding window + max_cross_region_ratio enforcement (ETA 90m)
- sylvie: implement model fallback rules for free/standard tiers in the routing layer + add metric tags (model.fallback=1) (ETA 2h)
- maria: add KV-cache short-circuit and report expected token savings (ETA 3h)
- infra oncall: consider temporary capacity burst (spin 2x small p3s) if traffic persists > 30m

sylvie: will add a canary gate: route 5% of free-tier overflow to eu-west first and monitor lat/err. if 95th latency > 500ms we rollback.

raj: small tweak to the policy above: set `max_cross_region_ratio` to 0.3 for model-heavy routes to avoid excessive egress bills.

kevin: noted. also we should emit a metric `routing.fallback_count` and tie it to billing alerts so finance sees impact.

maria: quick check — does Dedicated capacity bypass these fallbacks? we should respect dedicated contracts and not downgrade without approval.

kevin: yes Dedicated stays pinned. these rules only apply to Hosted and Shared capacity. documented in the policy snippet.

ops-bot: Update: temporary cluster add request submitted (2x p3-small in us-west) — ETA ~15m.

raj: cool. once we have the policy and canary we should run a short loadtest to validate fairness. I can stand up a synthetic load after the admission change.

kevin: thanks all — I’ll follow up in 2h with metrics. if anything spikes ping @sylvie and @raj directly. :thumbsup:
